units.title: Component 01: Exploring modern and literary heritage texts

topics.title: Section A: Modern prose or drama

outcomes.text: Respond to a studied modern prose or drama text (such as Animal Farm, An Inspector Calls or Never Let Me Go).
Discuss themes, ideas and issues in the modern text.
Discuss characters and relationships in the modern text.
Comment on the language of the modern text.
Explain how social or cultural context shapes the modern text, and note literary contexts such as symbolism or allegory.
Explain the significance of a word, phrase or sentence in its context.
Read at a literal level and also explore deeper implied meaning.
Explain characters' motivation, the sequence of events and how actions relate.
Identify and interpret key themes.
Give an informed personal response, backed by close reference to evidence in the text.
Reflect critically on the text using context, and accept that other valid readings exist.
Explain and illustrate how word choices shape meaning.
Analyse how the writer uses language, form and structure to create effects.
Use terminology such as phrase, metaphor, meter, irony and persona accurately.
Make connections and contrasts between the studied text and a thematically linked unseen modern extract of the same genre.
Compare features and qualities to deepen understanding of themes, characters, settings, contexts and styles.
Read widely among modern prose and drama to see how one text illuminates another.
Write clear, coherent extended responses to literature.
Choose and emphasise key points for a purpose, and keep a consistent viewpoint.
Weave quotations and references into the argument.
Write for varied purposes: describe, explain, summarise, argue, analyse and evaluate.
Use accurate Standard English, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
Respond to a studied 19th century novel (such as Great Expectations, Jane Eyre, A Christmas Carol or Jekyll and Hyde).
Discuss themes, ideas and issues in the novel.
Discuss atmosphere and emotion in the novel.
Trace plot development in the novel.
Discuss characters and relationships and the language of the novel.
Explain how social, historical, cultural or literary contexts such as the Gothic or science fiction shape the novel.
Explain the significance of a word, phrase or sentence in its context.
Tell literal from implied meaning in 19th century writing.
Explain motivation, the sequence of events and the links between actions.
Interpret key themes of an enduring 19th century text.
Support a personal view with close evidence from the text.
Use understanding of context to read critically, and recognise differing valid interpretations.
Explain how language choices shape meaning.
Analyse the writer's use of language, form and structure for effect.
Apply terminology including phrase, metaphor, meter, irony and persona.
Write a sustained, informed personal response to the novel.
Select and emphasise key points, keeping a consistent viewpoint.
Support views with well-chosen quotations and references.
Write to describe, explain, summarise, argue, analyse and evaluate.
Use accurate Standard English, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
Study one themed cluster of the OCR Poetry Anthology: Love and Relationships, Conflict, or Youth and Age.
Discuss themes, ideas and issues in poems since 1789.
Discuss atmosphere, tone and attitude in a poem.
Explain how poems appeal to the senses.
Analyse language and imagery in a poem.
Analyse form and structure in a poem.
Explain the significance of a word, phrase or line in context.
Tell literal from implied meaning in a poem.
Explain a speaker's motivation and how events or actions in a poem relate.
Identify and interpret key themes in poems.
Give an informed personal response backed by close reference to the poem.
Recognise that other readers may validly interpret a poem differently.
Explain how vocabulary choices and structural features shape meaning.
Analyse a poet's use of language, including figurative language, form and structure.
Use terms such as rhyming pattern, stanza form and imagery accurately.
Compare a studied poem from the cluster with a thematically linked unseen poem.
Make connections and contrasts between poems in themes, settings and styles.
Use a range of poems to see how one illuminates another.
Write clear, coherent, sustained responses to poems.
Select key points, keep a consistent viewpoint, and use quotations to support views.
Write for different purposes: describe, explain, summarise, argue, analyse and evaluate.
Use accurate Standard English, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
Respond to one studied play from Romeo and Juliet, The Merchant of Venice, Macbeth or Much Ado About Nothing.
Discuss themes, ideas and issues in the play.
Discuss atmosphere and emotion and plot development in the play.
Discuss characters, relationships and the language of the play.
Discuss dramatic effects in the play.
Explain the social, historical or cultural contexts shown in the play, such as social customs and attitudes.
Explain the significance of a word, phrase or sentence in context.
Tell literal from implied meaning in Shakespeare's language.
Explain motivation and the sequence and relationship of events.
Interpret key themes in a text written for performance.
Support an individual response with close reference to the play.
Use context to read critically and recognise other valid interpretations.
Explain how language choices shape meaning.
Analyse how Shakespeare's language, form and structure create effects.
Analyse dramatic devices used to engage and entertain an audience.
Use terminology including phrase, metaphor, meter, irony and persona accurately.
Write a sustained, informed personal response to the play.
Emphasise key points, keep a consistent viewpoint, and weave in textual references.
Write to describe, explain, summarise, argue, analyse and evaluate.
Use accurate Standard English, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
